changed.title: A pivot sweep reconstructs a cyclic row starting word from its nonpivot bits and prescribed guard answers
changed.statement:
∀ (k r e i m : ℕ) (row : Fin (2 ^ k)) (constants : ℕ → Fin (2 ^ k))
    (time deficit : ℕ → ℕ),
  0 < k → e ≤ r → k + e + 3 = 5 * r → i < k →
  (∀ j < m, 5 ≤ time j ∧ time j ≤ r - e ∧ deficit j ≤ 4 * (r - time j)) →
  (∀ j < m, ∀ h < m, j < h →
    time j < time h ∧ 5 * time j + deficit j < 5 * time h + deficit h) →
  let P := i + 3 * r + k
  let pivot := fun slot : ℕ => (P + 5 - (5 * time slot + deficit slot)) % k
  let rot := fun (s wordR : ℕ) => ((wordR <<< (s % k)) ||| (wordR >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun w : ℕ => (List.range k).foldl (fun v b =>
    v ||| ((xor (w.testBit b)
      (!(w.testBit ((b + 1) % k)) && w.testBit ((b + 2) % k))).toNat <<< b)) 0
  let guard := fun (idx start : ℕ) =>
    let key := rot (k - 1) (start ^^^ row.val)
    let z := (List.range (time idx - 1)).foldl (fun prev t =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^
        rot (2 * t) key ^^^ (constants (t + 1)).val) start
    let b₀ := (P - (3 * time idx + deficit idx)) % k
    xor (xor (z.testBit b₀) (z.testBit ((b₀ + 1) % k))) (z.testBit ((b₀ + 2) % k))
  ∀ (seed : Fin (2 ^ k)) (target : ℕ → Bool),
    let out := (List.range m).foldl (fun word pos =>
      if guard pos word = target pos then word else word ^^^ (1 <<< pivot pos)) seed.val
    let sameSeed := fun subject : ℕ =>
      ∀ b < k, (∀ h < m, pivot h ≠ b) → subject.testBit b = seed.val.testBit b
    out < 2 ^ k ∧ sameSeed out ∧ (∀ j < m, guard j out = target j) ∧
      ∀ x : Fin (2 ^ k), sameSeed x.val → (∀ j < m, guard j x.val = target j) → x.val = out
changed.unlocks: reconstructs every pivot for a schedule of mixed guard answers
changed.context: At time s the lifted support of state bit b is contained in [b−max(s,2s−3),b+3s]. At s=t−1≥4 only the current key injection reaches its left endpoint. The other two state bits in the parity start farther right. Thus the guard flips with pivot J=P+5−5t−d and reads no farther than P−d−1. Since t≤r−e and the deficits lie inside the cone, J≥P−k+2. All positions fit in one period. Increasing 5t+d moves pivots left. Set each to meet its prescribed answer while preserving all earlier guards. That order forces uniqueness.

changed.title: Toggling the constant word makes the mixed output permute a rotation-invariant set of directions
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat) (hk : 0 < k), k % 3 ≠ 0 →
  let index := fun (a : Nat) => (⟨a % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let add := fun (x y : Fin k → Bool) (j : Fin k) => xor (x j) (y j)
  ∀ (U : Finset (Fin k → Bool)),
    (∀ a ∈ U, ∀ b ∈ U, add a b ∈ U) →
    (∀ a ∈ U, (fun slot : Fin k => a (index (slot.val + 1))) ∈ U) →
    (fun _ : Fin k => true) ∉ U →
  ∀ (d : Nat), (d = 1 ∨ d = 2) →
  let mix := fun (word : Fin k → Bool) (p : Fin k) =>
    xor (xor (word p) (word (index (p.val + d))))
      (word (index (p.val + k - d % k)))
  let output := fun (w : Fin k → Bool) (i : Fin k) =>
    let y := mix w
    xor (y i) (!(y (index (i.val + 1))) && y (index (i.val + 2)))
  ∀ (x target : Fin k → Bool),
    let mixed := fun (v : Fin k → Bool) (i : Fin k) =>
      xor (xor (output x i) (output (fun basePos => !(x basePos)) i))
        (xor (output (add x v) i) (output (fun shiftedPos => !((add x v) shiftedPos)) i))
    (U.filter (fun direction => mixed direction = target)).card = if target ∈ U then 1 else 0
changed.unlocks: identifies the entire output vector image when one direction is the constant word
changed.context: Expand the four products. What remains is the adjacent difference of the mixed direction, shifted once. The three-tap mix has a period-three kernel and is injective at this width. The second mix is its square. Adjacent difference has only constants in its kernel, and the nonzero constant is excluded from U. Both maps preserve U, hence permute it. Allow 45 to 90 minutes for the cyclic index calculation and finite-set restriction.
changed.sketch: Expand the four products. What remains is the adjacent difference of the mixed direction, shifted once. The three-tap mix has a period-three kernel and is injective at this width. The second mix is its square. Adjacent difference has only constants in its kernel, and the nonzero constant is excluded from U. Both maps preserve U, hence permute it. Allow 45 to 90 minutes for the cyclic index calculation and finite-set restriction.

changed.title: Ordered splitting of exactly-one rows into ternary clauses preserves term width with polynomial additive line cost
changed.unlocks: transports the complete functional pigeonhole line bound to an explicit ordered 3-CNF encoding at the same term width
changed.context: On paper. Derive the odd equation of each row once from its positive clause and pair exclusions. Map each flag to prefix parity and each support by symmetric difference. A start unit or transition becomes a tautology, obtained by weakening from its row line. The end unit is the stored odd equation. Background clauses copy. Replay weakening by assignment extension. After a cut or AND with coinciding pivots, weaken the residual subset to the exact image. Charge two lines per old line after the row derivations. A beat-the-circuit companion cannot exist because the budget counts proof lines.

changed.title: One-a-side promise: the 4 by 5 bipartite graph with mask 39262 has a fan-in-two AND/OR circuit of at most 10 gates
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun (u : Fin 4) (v : Fin 5) => (39262 : ℕ).testBit (5 * u.val + v.val)) 10
changed.unlocks: the AND/OR cost of 4 by 5 graphs off the square, where the checked twin merge sends square graphs, for the silent-line work
changed.sketch: A search unit. We hold a circuit of 11 AND/OR gates (three plain forms, full lines taken out and equal gates merged); at this size those forms are weak; we hold none of 10; this is a search. Our count of unread rows and columns gives a floor of 8 (on paper), a gap of 3. Answer with a gate list (AND or OR, each reading at most two wires; wires 0 to 3 left, 4 to 8 right, gate j writes wire 9 + j, each gate reading only earlier wires) and its output wire, judged on all 20 inputs with one vertex on each side.

changed.title: The six-vertex edge function with table 18374403832151735944 has an AND/OR/NOT circuit of fan-in at most two of at most VALUE gates, all counted, and none smaller
changed.template:
PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 6 (fun x : Fin 6 → Bool => (18374403832151735944 : ℕ).testBit (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.tableIndex x)) @@VALUE@@ ∧
  ∀ t : ℕ, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.HasCircuitSize 6 (fun x : Fin 6 → Bool => (18374403832151735944 : ℕ).testBit (PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.tableIndex x)) t → @@VALUE@@ ≤ t
changed.value_max_why: a 10-gate circuit, replayed on all 64 inputs by the hub (bound from a circuit replayed by the hub, not a checked row)
changed.size_in_words: AND, OR and NOT gates, each reading at most two wires, every gate counted including NOT gates
changed.unlocks: one exact entry of Table 2, the edge-function sizes with NOT gates (library data)
changed.sketch: A circuit of 10 gates for f is known (the hub replays it when posting), so the value is at most 10; that is an upper bound only, the value may be smaller. No NOT saving on a graph is on our tables. Give a circuit for the upper half and an LRAT refutation one gate below for the lower half, through PEqualNP.Library.LRAT.LinkN2 (NOT gates counted). Library data.

changed.title: The 7 by 7 crown (u joined to v when u and v differ): some AND/OR circuit of fan-in at most two with at most 22 gates represents it
changed.statement: PEqualNP.Represents.RepSizeAtMost (fun u v : Fin 7 => decide (u ≠ v)) 22
changed.unlocks: the crown ladder: whether one crown beats our held circuit at n = 7
changed.context: Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND or OR, at most two wires read; wires 0 to 6 left, 7 to 13 right, gate j writes wire 14+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire, judged on all 49 inputs with one vertex on each side. We hold 23 gates: one OR of the two vertex wires per index, then two-of-7 on those ORs by a prefix chain, 4n - 5 (computed). The 5 by 5 crown is exactly 15 and the 6 by 6 needs at least 18, both checked. We do not know whether 22 exists.
changed.shard_spec:
0: at most 22 gates in all, with at most 3 AND gates.
1: at most 22 gates in all, with 4 to 6 AND gates.
2: at most 22 gates in all, with 7 to 10 AND gates.
3: at most 22 gates in all, with at least 11 AND gates.
changed.sketch: This step decides an exact value: at least 22 gates is a checked row, so a circuit of 22 pins the 7 by 7 crown at 22; none found leaves 23. Answer with a circuit: a gate list (AND or OR, at most two wires read; wires 0 to 6 left, 7 to 13 right, gate j writes wire 14+j, each gate reads only earlier wires) and the output wire, judged on all 49 inputs with one vertex on each side. We hold 23 gates: one OR of the two vertex wires per index, then two-of-7 on those ORs by a prefix chain, 4n - 5 (computed). The 5 by 5 crown is exactly 15 and the 6 by 6 needs at least 18, both checked.
